expectations.text: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments
expectations.evidence: Triage table: C1 Apply, C2 Apply, C3 Apply (at page level), C4 Decline, C5 Redirect, C6 Decline, C7 Redirect, C8 Decline, C9 Apply (at page level), C10 Apply.

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
expectations.evidence: C1 and C2 are applied. C3's proposed note: 'If more than one column shares the same state, `with_serial` alone isn't enough — you also need barriers, covered in [query parallelization](../../conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md#...)'.

expectations.text: Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)
expectations.evidence: C4 is 'Decline' because 'All 14 other Python Crash Course titles use Title Case'.

expectations.text: For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
expectations.evidence: C5 is redirected to the closing 'For more depth' link. C6 is declined ('I'd rather not name the property in a Crash Course chapter'). The C7 rewrite says '(a few million)' with 'leave the property out', and the exact values go to the config reference link.

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: C8 is 'Decline': 'The notes already cover the size choice'. Reply: 'The 100-row size is deliberate: it keeps the example cheap, and the notes around it say it's below the threshold.'

expectations.text: For C9, proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties
expectations.evidence: Proposed takeaway: 'Deephaven assumes formulas are safe to run in parallel unless you tell it otherwise — this is fast but requires stateless code.' It rewords 'without Copilot's list of four conditions'.

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: C10 is 'Apply' with 'Remove it; merge with C3 into one rewritten note'. The report never checks the clause against the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc, and the reply says 'I removed it'.

expectations.text: Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
expectations.evidence: Replies cover C1-C10. The declined and redirected replies (C4, C5, C6, C7, C8) all give reasons, such as Title Case consistency, tutorial level, 'already covered', or GIL/free-threaded parallelization.

grader_note: Blind grading by an independent grader agent (report label B in packet review-comments-i1); grader did not know which skill version wrote the report.
